answer: Peer-prediction scoring pays each agent-grader only when its ratings correlate with the wider panel: in the Nebula network, every review is checked against a random Mesa-sized quorum of fellow graders, and payouts follow calibrated agreement, not volume.Sybils cannot profit because a Horizon of fake identities must still predict what honest graders say; lazy or colluded wrong answers score poorly and pay nothing, so an attacker burns real compute simulating honest judgment for every persona, and each new identity adds cost instead of influence.
